result.summary: This PR fixes a bug in CTxMemPool::removeForReorg where transactions with BIP68 relative-locktime sequences and mempool (unconfirmed) parent inputs cache stale LockPoints that are not correctly invalidated after invalidateblock lowers the chain tip, causing valid transactions and their descendants to be wrongly evicted. The final fix recalculates lockpoints via CalculateLockPointsAtTip whenever either the cached validity check or the sequence-lock check fails, evicting only if the fresh check also fails, replacing an earlier genesis-sentinel-detection approach that missed mixed confirmed/unconfirmed input cases. A new functional test covers BIP68-disabled, height-based, mixed-input, and time-based (MTP-drop) scenarios.
result.problem: Wallets, exchanges, and second-layer protocols that rely on transactions remaining in the mempool after a reorg can lose valid unconfirmed transactions (and their descendants) unexpectedly, forcing rebroadcast and potentially breaking dependent protocol assumptions. This mirrors a previously fixed issue for TRUC transactions (#33504).

resolved_concerns: Bicaru20 suggested moving the genesis-sentinel check into TestLockPointValidity; author found it breaks an internal assert and kept the check at the caller, Bicaru20 agreed after reproducing the failure.

ismaelsadeeq identified that the original fix missed transactions with mixed confirmed/unconfirmed inputs; author adopted ismaelsadeeq's suggested general-recalculation approach and extended the test.
instagibbs raised the missing time-based (MTP-drop) variant; Bicaru20 and author collaborated to design a deterministic test for it and added it.
Bicaru20 nits on assert_equal usage and an unnecessary extra block in the test were both addressed in later pushes.

result.card: This PR fixes a mempool bug where BIP68 transactions with unconfirmed (mempool) parent inputs cache stale LockPoints that are not properly invalidated when invalidateblock lowers the chain tip, causing valid transactions and their descendants to be wrongly evicted from the mempool. The fix, refined through review, recalculates lockpoints whenever either the cached validity or sequence-lock check fails and evicts only if the fresh check also fails, correctly handling all-unconfirmed, mixed confirmed/unconfirmed, and time-based (MTP) cases. Bortlesboat independently confirmed the regression exists on master and is fixed here; ismaelsadeeq (member) identified a gap in the author's original genesis-sentinel approach and proposed the adopted general fix, followed by re-ACKs from Bicaru20. Discussion is fully resolved with no open objections, and the PR closes issue #35007. This mirrors a previously fixed issue class for TRUC transactions (#33504), suggesting a recurring category of stale-lockpoint bugs worth eliminating.
